The correction is a null result: all three baseline populations confirmed sound, delta 0; the parent's acceptance verdict is unchanged.

completion_data.completion_summary: Recaptured the corpus baseline figures the parent record's net-deletion acceptance criterion is measured against. Determination: the correction is a null result (delta 0 for NET-PROD, NET-TEST and NET-MD baselines) — the parent's authoritative acceptance figure (Instrument B, NET-TOTAL +1,219 against the -10,000 floor) was never exposed to the probe's undercounting defect and remains unchanged. Both parent plan files annotated with per-figure determinations; the Phase-20 Instrument A field-set ambiguity was resolved via git ancestry evidence.

memory_candidates.content: When a corpus-size probe is later found to undercount (e.g. tracked-only git ls-files enumeration blind to untracked files), bounding a frozen historical baseline's exposure retroactively is possible without the file itself ever being recoverable: enumerate the superset of files first-committed after the baseline's capture commit (git log --diff-filter=A), then narrow by checking for any OTHER commit (any task) within a tight time bracket around the exact capture instant. If no concurrent writer has any commit in that bracket, there is no evidence a second writer's uncommitted work existed on disk at that instant, and the narrowed untracked-at-capture set can be confirmed empty even when the raw superset is large.

To resolve whether a recorded tool-output line came from a fixed or stale copy of a script when the line is missing an expected field, three corroborating checks settle it without re-running anything: (1) git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-commit> <reading's-own-commit> confirms the fix was in history by that point; (2) the commit's own message (e.g. mentions 'redeploy') may directly state the copy was refreshed; (3) git show <commit>:<path> on the source file confirms the fix's code is literally present. All three agreeing settles 'fields trimmed when recorded' vs 'stale copy used' definitively.
